reason: Selected controlled planning comparison supports a cost-aware interactive-planning check, while proposed richer feedback remains untested.

candidates.title: Compare interactive planning with direct and symbolic baselines
candidates.rule: For structured symbolic planning, compare a step-wise LLM tool loop with direct plan generation and a classical planner under the same deadline before assuming interaction improves planning.
candidates.passage: The direct and agentic approaches produce plans of nearly identical length
candidates.location: Sections V–VI; main comparison and limitations
candidates.finding: On 102 Blocksworld instances under 180 seconds, direct Haiku planning solves 63.7%, the interactive version 66.7%, and Fast Downward 85.3%. The interactive version costs 5.7 times more tokens per solution.
candidates.conditions: Interactive planning receives action-applicability and resulting-state feedback with reset/retry. Compare plan quality on co-solved cases separately from total success.
candidates.limitations: One run per instance and one model tier; variance is unknown. State transitions are externally observed even though no explicit goal-distance signal is supplied. Neither the memorization account nor benefits of adding goal-distance feedback are experimentally established.
candidates.validation_test: Use repeated seeds and unfamiliar domain variants; compare success, valid-plan length and spend under matched deadlines. Test richer progress feedback as a separate ablation rather than assuming it explains the result.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
